subject: Relation between Categorical and Multinomial Distributions for Order Categorical Regression

messages.author: d1237c2d244e29ff
messages.subject: Relation between Categorical and Multinomial Distributions for Order Categorical Regression
parts:
In Stan we can write an ordered logistic model with a single ecological-level predictor:
for (n in 1:N){
Outcome[n] ~ ordered_logistic( (Beta[1] + Beta[2]*X[Cluster[n]]), C);
}

Which is short for the more explicit model:
for (n in 1:N) {
real eta;
eta <- Beta[1] + Beta[2]*X[Cluster[n]];
scrap[1] <- 1 - inv_logit(eta - C[1]);
for (k in 2:(K-1))
scrap[k] <- inv_logit(eta - C[k-1]) - inv_logit(eta - C[k]);
scrap[K] <- inv_logit(eta - C[K-1]);
Outcome[n] ~ categorical(scrap);
}

Now, the question is... since the predictor is at the ecological level, could we re-write the model for efficiency by rewriting the individual-level data at the cluster level... so instead of the data looking like:
Outcome[1] = 3
Outcome[2] = 5
etc...

We have cluster-level counts as vectors, defined simply by summing the number of outcomes of each category in the given cluster:
OutcomeCluster[1] = (10, 3, 50, 30, 2)'
OutcomeCluster[2] = (12, 45, 40, 35, 4)'

And then change the model to:
for (l in 1:L) {
real eta;
eta <- Beta[1] + Beta[2]*X[l];
scrap[1] <- 1 - inv_logit(eta - C[1]);
for (k in 2:(K-1))
scrap[k] <- inv_logit(eta - C[k-1]) - inv_logit(eta - C[k]);
scrap[K] <- inv_logit(eta - C[K-1]);
OutcomeCluster[l] ~ multinomial(scrap);
}

In other words... instead of updating the LP accumulator N times with the categorical distribution, can we update it only L times with the multinomial, since the categorical distribution is just a special case of the multinomial with count equals 1?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Relation between Categorical and Multinomial Distributions for Order Categorical Regression
parts:
Yes --- you can rewrite categorical or ordered_logistic using
multinomial. Same thing with the Bernoulli and binomial.

We should probably have a multinomial version of the ordered
categorical. Maybe Rob will put it on his growing list of GLM
optimizations to take on --- I know they're redoing the ordered
logistic itself to make it faster.

- Bob

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Relation between Categorical and Multinomial Distributions for Order Categorical Regression
parts:
Careful — there’s a subtle difference in the normalizing constant
depending on whether or not you have N realizations of the same
process (binomial or mulitnomial) or N parallel discrete processes
(a product of Bernoulli’s or a product of categoricals). I don’t think
it will affect sampling for any model we can specify but it’s something
to keep in mind.

For more see the Wikipedia entry,
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Categorical_distribution#Terminology.
